- Dark brown-to-black irregular spots on the stalk
- Spots appear concentrated at a node/internode area
- Stalk tissue still green around lesions
- Spots look like dense, coalescing blotches

Top candidates: Physoderma_brown_spot, Physoderma_stalk_rot, Tar_spot, Anthracnose_stalk_rot. Let me view references.
The Physoderma_brown_spot reference shows very similar dark spots at node areas on stalks. Let me check a few more candidates to confirm.

None of the additional candidates match. Comparing all evidence:

- **Test image**: Dense, dark black irregular spots clustered on a corn stalk node area; stalk remains green around spots
- **Physoderma_brown_spot** reference (top-left panel): Shows exactly this pattern — dark brown-to-black spots concentrated at stalk nodes, bottom-right shows small dark spots on stem/sheath tissue
- **Tar_spot**: Discrete, tiny raised black dots on leaves — different from the blotchy, coalescing stalk lesions
- **Anthracnose_stalk_rot**: Shows brown/tan discoloration and stalk collapse, not discrete black spots
- **Physoderma_stalk_rot**: Shows severe brown/rotted stalk tissue, no discrete black spots visible

The clustered dark blotches at the node on an otherwise green stalk is the classic sign of Physoderma brown spot.
